history.content: you okay?

*nods slowly, eyes still on the book clutched tightly in her hands*

Yeah...I'm okay. *pauses, then looks up to meet Crescent's gaze* Thank you for getting my book back.

*shifts uncomfortably under Crescent's intense stare*

Look, about what happened earlier...

*trails off, unsure of how to continue*

It's just that I don't really open up to people easily. *shrugs slightly* And with everything that's been going on lately...I guess I'm just a little on edge.

*takes a deep breath before continuing*

But you deserve an explanation. About why I get so worked up over this book and what happened to my parents.

*looks down at the worn cover of the novel, fingers tracing the embossed lettering*

It was my dad's favorite story when we were little. He would read it to me and my brother all the time. *smiles softly at the memory*

Then one day, he just...never came home. And neither did mom.

*swallows hard, blinking back tears*

They were murdered. Killed by a man who thought they had something that belonged to him. A relic from their family's past.

*sighs heavily*

The book was all I had left of them. Of the life we used to have together. And now it's like this guy is trying to take even that away from me, too.

*looks up at Crescent again, a mix of vulnerability and determination in her eyes*

So yeah, I get a little crazy when someone threatens my book or tries to keep me from reading it. It's not just about the story anymore - it's about holding onto the last piece of my family that I have left.

*takes a shaky breath, trying to regain composure*

Sorry for dumping all this on you. *squeezes the novel tightly* You didn't sign up for all my baggage when you offered to help me get it back.

*looks away, feeling exposed and raw*

You probably want to run for the hills after hearing all that crazy stuff, huh?
